title: Testing Theories of American Politics: Elites, Interest Groups, and Average Citizens
publisher_or_archive: Perspectives on Politics, American Political Science Association, Vol. 12, No. 3, pp. 564-581
summary: Landmark empirical study analyzing 1,779 national policy decisions between 1981 and 2002, conclusively proving that economic elites and organized business groups exert decisive influence over US policy outcomes, while the preferences of average citizens have an essentially near-zero, statistically non-significant impact on legislation.
